title: Generate a String With Characters That Have Odd Counts
statement: Build and return a string of length `n` made only of lowercase English letters, in which every letter that appears at all appears an odd number of times. Many strings qualify; any one of them is accepted.
notes:
## Intuition

Only the parity of each letter's count matters, so the simplest strings use as few letters as possible. If `n` is odd, one letter repeated `n` times already has an odd count. If `n` is even, a single letter would have an even count, but splitting `n` into `n - 1` (odd) copies of one letter and `1` copy of another gives two odd counts. No search over strings is needed.

## Approach

1. Set `oddCount` to `n` when `n` is odd and to `n - 1` when it is even; either way it is odd.
2. Append `'a'` to `result` `oddCount` times.
3. If that leaves one character missing (`oddCount < n`), append a single `'b'`, whose count of 1 is odd.
4. Return `result`.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 4` is even, so `oddCount = 3`. The loop builds `"aaa"`. Since `3 < 4`, one `'b'` is appended, giving `"aaab"`: `'a'` appears 3 times and `'b'` once, both odd. LeetCode shows `"pppz"`, which has the same shape with other letters; both are accepted.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): exactly `n` characters are appended.
- Space: O(n) for the returned string (no other storage).

## Pitfalls

- For even `n`, returning `n` copies of one letter fails, because `n` is an even count.
- Using `n / 2` copies of each of two letters also fails whenever `n / 2` is even (for example `n = 4`).
- The extra character must be a different letter; another `'a'` would just make `n` copies of `'a'`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `oddCount` | how many copies of `'a'` to use: the largest odd number not above `n` |
| `result` | the string being built |
| `i` | loop counter for the copies of `'a'` |

narration.2: Pick an odd count for 'a': n itself if n is odd, otherwise n - 1.
narration.5: ...so 'a' ends up with an odd count.
